input.note:
**Root cause:** The platform-base chart v2.0.3 introduced `automountServiceAccountToken: false` at the Pod spec level as a security-hardening default [cite: concepts/security/application-security-checklist#service-account-0]. This prevents the kubelet from mounting the service account token at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token` [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account#opt-out-of-api-credential-automounting-0].

**Evidence:**
1. The crashing pod `job-dispatcher-7b6f9c4d8-zk5np` (chart v2.0.3) has `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and only the `tmp` volume mount — no service account token volume.
2. The healthy pod `job-dispatcher-5d8b7c9f6d-q7m2x` (chart v1.8.0) has the `kube-api-access-7xq2d` volume mounted at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount`.
3. The crash log is conclusive: `FATAL unable to load in-cluster configuration: open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: no such file or directory`

`job-dispatcher` uses the Kubernetes in-cluster client and therefore requires the service account token to be present.

**Fix:** In your chart values for `job-dispatcher`, explicitly set `automountServiceAccountToken: true`. Because the Pod spec value takes precedence over the ServiceAccount-level value [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account#opt-out-of-api-credential-automounting-1], this will override the chart's new default and cause the kubelet to mount the token as a projected volume [cite: concepts/security/service-accounts#assign-to-pod-0], restoring normal startup. After applying the updated values and completing the rollout, the old pod will be terminated and the new one will be healthy.
